- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 85), model frequently overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +5% above peak for next 7 days.  
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 75), model often lags; adjust forecast downward by 2–4% for next 3 days.  
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overfit recent volatility; smooth 30d forecast by averaging last 10d price + sentiment-weighted trend.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.67, 0.33, 0.67), model often misreads momentum; apply 1–2% dampening to forecast if sentiment oscillates.
